messages:
maria: quick thread — ran into head-of-line stalls on staging while testing eager warmup + safetensors sharded bundles. low-priority prefetch kept getting starved when many 1-shot requests came through.
julian: can you paste the logs? are we seeing IO queue saturation or runtime backpressure?
maria: logs show repeated 'prefetch queue full' warnings from WarmupManager and then long waits for KV init. stack: warmup -> weightcache -> runtime.
priya: are those safetensors bundles with per-shard index files, or single large file? that affects our ability to partially map.
maria: per-shard .safetensors, 128 shards, each ~40MB. manifest includes checksum + preferred-load-mode. we attempted eager=hotstart.
samir: recent change: WarmupManager treats any shard > 32MB as "async-copy" which uses our copy queue. maybe the threshold is wrong.
maria: yeah. proposal: add adaptive throttling to prefetch: measure average copy latency and queue depth, then reduce parallelism when latency > 120ms. fallback to memory-map if copy latency high.
julian: that sounds reasonable. also need to expose a backpressure signal from runtime -> caller so route layer can throttle incoming requests rather than piling up prefetch. e.g., a 503-ish transient hint or internal metric.
priya: we should avoid surface 503 to customers. internal route policy could queue at gateway and opt for on-demand lazy load for short requests. Maybe add a "prefetch_budget" header on internal RPC that the gateway can decrement.
warmup-bot: NOTE: observed 74% increase in token-latency variance when prefetch queue depth topped out (experiment 2026-02-14).
samir: implementation detail: WeightSource API should add two methods: `prefetch_hint(shard_id, priority)` and `get_loading_mode(shard_meta)` returning ["mmap","async-copy","direct-disk"]. keep backward compat by defaulting to existing heuristic.
maria: agreed. also add a light-weight async metric: `expected_ready_epoch(shard_id)` so scheduler can decide can-i-wait.
julian: tradeoffs: mmap avoids copy but can thrash page cache and cause GC-like stalls on memory-constrained hosts. async-copy is expensive on PCIe. adaptive policy needs to consider host memory pressure + PCIe bandwidth + request latency SLO.
priya: TTL-based cache eviction + soft-priority for embeddings-heavy routes could reduce churn. For Dedicated customers we could expose a config knob: `warmup.prefer_mmap=true|false`.
samir: what about safety & format compatibility? if we add a tiny per-shard sidecar index (e.g., .sidx) with a version byte, loaders can fall back safely to older behavior if index missing. sample index format:
```
{"version":1, "shard_id": 12, "preferred_load":"mmap", "kv_ranges": [[0,4096],[4096,8192]]}
```
maria: yes — keep it optional. fallback order: sidx preferred -> manifest override -> runtime heuristic.
julian: let's also add a short-circuit for small hot shards: if shard_size < 8MB and request concurrency < 4, prefetch eagerly with high priority. That reduces 95th percentile for small models.
priya: operational runbook note: when prefetch queue full, trigger gauge alert and temporarily lower gateway concurrency for that model-version. avoid host OOM.
maria: action items: (1) samir PR to WeightSource API + sidx parser, (2) julian add runtime backpressure metric & gateway header, (3) priya update warmup config knobs + runbook. I'll instrument experiment with adaptive threshold 120ms -> 200ms.
samir: will open PR today with tests for missing sidx and compatibility fallback.
warmup-bot: REMINDER: canary run scheduled 2165435700 for model=redwood/llama-2-7b-shard128.
maria: thanks — keeping an eye on it. :thumbsup:
